risks.risk: Business risk - dependence on the Indian automotive industry cycle
risks.note: "The operations of the Company are directly dependent on the growth of the Indian automotive industry", so any moderation in vehicle demand flows straight through to the Company.

risks.risk: Financial risk - supply chain disruption and raw material availability
risks.note: "Any disruption of supply chain, availability of raw material could potentially impact the financial position and earnings of the Company."

The Company is currently operating primarily under a single business segment manufacturing seat frames and seat trims for passenger cars and utility vehicles, leaving no diversification cushion within the existing business.
Sale of products in the related-party disclosure is essentially all to associate Bharat Seats Limited, so the revenue base is tied to a single group counterparty.

risks.risk: Segment-mix and demand normalisation across vehicle categories
risks.note: India's automotive industry in FY2025 reflected a normalisation pattern - two-wheelers recovered only gradually with rural demand sensitive to income cycles and financing, and commercial vehicles moderated in line with freight cycle normalisation.

risks.risk: Powertrain transition - electrification reshaping platform requirements
risks.note: BEV adoption alongside a resurgence of HEVs and PHEVs, plus expanded safety and fuel-economy regulation, continues to reshape platform requirements for component makers.

risks.risk: Structural competitiveness constraints of the Indian auto component sector
risks.note: India's share of the $20 billion global automotive component trade remains modest at around 3%; operational costs, infrastructural gaps, moderate integration into global value chains and limited R&D expenditure continue to constrain competitiveness.

risks.risk: Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty affecting demand and supply chains
risks.note: "The Automobile industry will closely monitor macroeconomic factors and global geopolitics, which will determine the key demand conditions and supply chain dynamics going forward"; trade tensions, tighter financial conditions and geopolitical stress were flagged for 2025.

risks.risk: Execution risk on new subsidiaries and joint venture
risks.note: The two wholly owned subsidiaries and the NDR Hayashi joint venture formed during FY26 had all yet to commence operations at year-end, so the new seat-insert-fabric, NVH and southern component projects remain unproven.

one-line thesis: NDR Auto reported record Q4 EBITDA margins (11.9%) and a historic order book of INR 650 Cr (+INR 200 Cr QoQ), driven entirely by new Maruti Suzuki models. The strategic pivot into higher-value electronics (ambient lighting, latches) and seat frame localization positions the company to double revenue by FY30, though near-term margins may face startup costs from new capex.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 229.9 Cr (Q4, +19% YoY), INR 825.5 Cr (FY26, +15% YoY); EBITDA: INR 27.4 Cr (Q4, +25% YoY), Margin 11.90% (Record High); PAT: INR 18.5 Cr (Q4), INR 61.9 Cr (FY26, +16% YoY); Order Book: INR 650 Cr (Record High, +INR 200 Cr QoQ); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but positive operating cash flow of INR 37.1 Cr reported (correcting prior filing error); One-offs: Increase in 'other expenses' due to project/R&D spend; Employee costs up 33% due to hiring for expansion.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Similar trajectory to FY26 expected for FY27, with long-term target of INR 3,000 Cr by FY30 (excluding Bharat Seats); Margin: Current ~11.5% EBITDA deemed sustainable, though new product startups may introduce temporary costs; Order Inflow: Strong visibility from Maruti Suzuki new models; Capex/Commissioning: Hayashi JV production delayed to June 2026 (from April) due to operational issues; New product lines (seat inserts, latches) ramping from Jan 2027.
order book & pipeline: INR 650 Cr as of March 31, 2026. Entire INR 200 Cr QoQ increase attributed to new Maruti Suzuki models. Existing order book reduced by eVitara as it entered production. Book covers programs executable over the next 3 years, with revenue impact extending to FY30.
segment / subsidiary detail: Core: Seat covers and frames. New Growth Engines: Ambient lighting (INR 10-20 Cr initial revenue), seat latches, seat belt reminder systems, seat inserts. Sunshade business (INR 20 Cr revenue) transferred to Hayashi JV. Premiumization trend (artificial leather, power/ventilated seats) expected to increase content value by 40-50% over 5 years.
growth verticals / optionality: Winning market share from competitors within Maruti Suzuki portfolio; Expansion into non-seating electronics (ambient lighting precursor to more); Geographic expansion via Aurangabad land bank to cater to Toyota and other OEMs; Potential to replicate seat business model in new locations.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin improved 100 bps QoQ due to product mix and volume discounts from vendors; Commodity costs indexed, limiting downside risk; EBITDA margin of 11.9% considered sustainable; Near-term pressure possible from startup costs of new capacities; Employee costs rising structurally to support growth.
capex / expansion: Total project cost for JV approved at INR 80 Cr (INR 30 Cr invested so far); Additional INR 30-40 Cr capex planned for FY27 for existing order book execution; INR 150 Cr total capex plan for new product lines (seat inserts, lighting, etc.); Land banks secured (26 acres Aurangabad, 9 acres Kharkhoda) to reduce future setup costs.
capital allocation: Phase-wise investment in JV based on order wins; Organic capacity expansion for new product lines; Acquisition of Delhi office (INR 12 Cr); Support to subsidiaries (INR 6 Cr); No dividend or buyback commentary provided.
risks & watch-items: Customer Concentration: Entire recent order book growth from Maruti Suzuki; Execution Risk: Delays in JV commissioning (Hayashi) and new product ramp-ups; Competition: Aggressive bidding for new OEM mandates; Margin Volatility: Startup costs for new facilities; Dependency on single OEM's volume performance.
management quality / tone: Optimistic and confident; Highlighted record metrics and strong OEM relationships; Cautious on specific near-term guidance due to ramp-up uncertainties but firm on long-term INR 3,000 Cr target; Transparent about filing errors and operational delays.
non-obvious takeaways: The entire INR 200 Cr order book growth is from Maruti Suzuki, indicating a significant share gain from a competitor rather than diversification; The company corrected a regulatory filing error regarding negative operating cash flow, clarifying it was actually positive INR 37 Cr; Ambient lighting orders are currently small (INR 10-20 Cr) but viewed as a strategic foothold for larger electronics penetration.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Company's operations are directly dependent on the growth of the Indian automotive industry
- India's growth profile continues to be supported by infrastructure spending, services strength and steady manufacturing activity, creating a structurally attractive environment for engineering-intensive companies
- Passenger vehicles remained supported by GST moderation, SUV-led mix, urban consumption resilience and expanding model portfolios; two-wheelers showed gradual recovery; commercial vehicles moderated with freight cycle normalisation
- Per-capita ownership of cars, scooters and tractors is much below global averages, which as the economy grows should lead to healthy demand for vehicles
- GST optimisation has lowered prices for the retail buyer, positively impacting the market
- IHS forecasts India light vehicle production CAGR of ~5% between 2025-30 versus a global average of 1%; India is one of the few regions where both ICE vehicles and EVs are expected to grow well over the next 3-5 years
- EV adoption is expected to rise on environmental concerns and government incentives, while HEVs and PHEVs have seen a resurgence as they cut emissions without relying on yet-to-be-developed charging infrastructure
- Industrial supply chains face more selective capital flows and a higher premium on reliability, quality execution and localisation
- Structural constraints on Indian auto components - India's share of the $20 billion global component trade is around 3%, with operational costs, infrastructural gaps, limited global value-chain integration and limited R&D spend constraining competitiveness
- The automobile industry will closely monitor macroeconomic factors and global geopolitics, which will determine demand conditions and supply chain dynamics going forward

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics

On May 09, 2025 the Board approved forming a 50:50 JV company with Hayashi Telempu Corporation, Japan - NDR Hayashi Automotive India Private Limited - for the manufacture of auto components, mainly NVH parts, ambient lighting, tonneau cover and rear shade. On August 11, 2025 the Board approved setting up a manufacturing facility for frame structures, seat covers (trims) and other plastic/metal/polyurethane-based automotive components, for which the Company formed a wholly owned subsidiary, NDR Auto Components South Private Limited. risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Customer Concentration: Entire recent order book growth from Maruti Suzuki; Execution Risk: Delays in JV commissioning (Hayashi) and new product ramp-ups; Competition: Aggressive bidding for new OEM mandates; Margin Volatility: Startup costs for new facilities; Dependency on single OEM's volume performance.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: The entire INR 200 Cr order book growth is from Maruti Suzuki, indicating a significant share gain from a competitor rather than diversification; The company corrected a regulatory filing error regarding negative operating cash flow, clarifying it was actually positive INR 37 Cr; Ambient lighting orders are currently small (INR 10-20 Cr) but viewed as a strategic foothold for larger electronics penetration.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Remain focused on a single business segment - manufacturing seat frames and seat trims for passenger cars and utility vehicles
- Pursue the newer verticals and opportunities that electrification is expected to open up for auto component manufacturers over the next decade
- Recruit for the right skills, raise competency through training and development, and recognise and reward leadership and performance to retain talent
- Extend quality assurance upstream by horizontal deployment of learnings and training at supplier partners
- Keep Health, Safety and Environment as a top priority, with periodic …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Competitor losing share within Maruti Suzuki portfolio due to NDR's superior cost, quality, and delivery. | Unlisted Tier-1 Seating Competitor | loser | High | Management explicitly stated they are gaining share from a specific vendor who is losing ground. |
| Rising content per vehicle due to premiumization (power/ventilated seats, electronics). | Bharat Seats (Associate) | beneficiary | Med | NDR holds 28% stake; Bharat Seats benefits from same premiumization trends and order book growth; Guidance raised to INR 3,500 Cr by FY30. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Order book] "Order book as on June 30, 2026, stands at Rs. 650 crore".
- [New JV] NDR Hayashi Automotive India Pvt. Ltd. (NHI), a JV with Hayashi Telempu Corporation Japan formed in 2025, to manufacture NVH floor carpet, dash inner, rear shade, tonneau cover, ambient lighting and other automotive interior/exterior components including floor mats.
- [Sector outlook] Deck cites healthy domestic demand, PV recovery, resilient exports, increasing vehicle content, premiumization and OEM capacity expansion; adds "Moderating commodity prices are also expected to gradually translate to lower raw material prices for the industry".
- [Regulatory/one-off] FY ended 31st Mar 2026 carried an exceptional item, "Statutory impact of new Labour Codes", of 64.75 (0.08%) in the P&L statement; nil in each quarter shown.
